newsitem.title: USA: SabreTech closes second Florida facility.
newsitem.headline: SabreTech closes second Florida facility.

text.p: SabreTech Inc., an aircraft repair company implicated in the crash last May of a ValuJet flight near Miami, has agreed to surrender a Federal Aviation Administration certificate for its Orlando repair station rather than have the FAA shut the facility down.
The FAA, in a statement early Saturday, said SabreTech had agreed to give back the certificate Friday after a two-month FAA investigation of the Orlando plant.

The FAA said it had been prepared to allege that SabreTech falsified records by signing off work that was not actually performed; failed to have the proper tools, equipment and materials required for repairs it performed; and performed maintenance without proper manuals.
The agency said it had been prepared to issue an emergency order revoking the company's certification to do business at the Orlando facility.

Revocation of an FAA certificate is the strictest enforcement action available to the agency. To resume regulated activities, the company will be required to complete the full recertification process, the FAA said.

SabreTech said in a statement Friday night that it was handing back its Orlando repair station certificate "out of an abundance of caution" and asking the FAA for a complete recertification of the facility.

The company said earlier this month that it was trying to sell its Miami facility, where in May an employee mislabeled as "empty" dozens of oxygen cannisters that were shipped aboard ill-fated ValuJet Flight 592. A suspected cause of the May 11 crash, which killed 110 people, was the accidental activation of the oxygen generators, which can produce extreme heat.
SabreTech's Miami repair station surrendered its FAA certificate earlier this week, citing the impact on its business of bad publicity from the ValuJet crash.
SabreTech, one of the nation's largest aircraft maintenance contractors, is a Phoenix, Arizona-based division of privately owned Saberliner Corp. of St. Louis.
The FAA said it would begin more "in-depth" examinations of SabreTech operations in Texas and Arizona in the coming two weeks.
